question: Which world heritage site was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sun Temple, also known as the Konark Sun Temple, is located in Konark, Odisha, India.
 
• It was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
 
• The temple is designed in the shape of a colossal chariot, having elaborately carved stone wheels, pillars, and walls.
 
• It is dedicated to the Hindu Sun God, Surya, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eastern Ganga dynasty:**

 
 
• The Eastern Ganga dynasty was a medieval Indian dynasty that ruled the region of Kalinga (present-day Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh) from the 11th century to the early 15th century.
 
• They are renowned for their patronage of art and architecture, particularly the construction of temples.
 
 
 
• **Konark Sun Temple:**
 
 
• The Konark Sun Temple is one of the most well-known temples in India, famous for its unique architecture and intricate carvings.
 
• The temple was conceived as a gigantic chariot of the Sun God, with twelve pairs of exquisitely ornamented wheels being pulled by seven horses.
 
• The temple's architecture and iconography reflect the sophistication of the Ganga dynasty's engineering and artistic capabilities.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• A UNESCO World Heritage Site is a landmark or area with legal protection by an international convention administered by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).
 
• The sites are designated as having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance, and are deemed important for the collective interests of humanity.
 
• The Konark Sun Temple was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984 for its architectural grandeur and historical significance.
